We are constantly forced to sort through mounds of substandard, spoiled, and dangerously expired goods, a clear sign that no one, absolutely no one, who works here gives the slightest damn about what they are selling.

​But the real, crushing hopelessness sets in when you deal with the management. After enduring the grim spectacle of their inventory, you raise a complaint, and what you get back is a black hole of apathy. The management is a complete and utter void. Multiple, desperate attempts to inform them of these health hazards—the mold, the outdated items—have been met with the silent, soul-crushing message: Your health does not matter. Your complaint means nothing.

​It is utterly degrading to spend money here knowing that the very people responsible for your purchase are actively ignoring the risk of selling you something that could make you sick. This branch is a pathetic joke, a miserable failure of retail responsibility, and should be shut down before their negligence actually hospitalizes someone. Avoid this depressing health trap at all costs.
